Before voice mode starts, here is who hears you.
Before dictation starts, here is who hears you.

Your voice streams straight to OpenAI’s realtime model, using your computer’s ChatGPT sign-in or API key. OpenAI also gets the session’s recent messages and tool results as context. Your computer gets what you say and pi’s replies.
When realtime voice isn’t available, your computer turns your speech into text and may speak replies, using the speech services it is set up with (OpenAI or another provider).
The recording goes to your computer, which transcribes it with its speech service and tidies the text with its AI model. Either may be OpenAI or another provider.
The developer of pi never receives your audio or text. Traffic between this phone and your computer is end-to-end encrypted.
Each provider handles what it gets under its own privacy policy. You can turn this off any time in voice settings or the menu.
